frames.narration: The user types 'c'. The page waits briefly to see whether more keys follow, then asks the CDN for suggestions for the prefix 'c'.
'c' is the hottest prefix there is, so the CDN already has the answer from a moment ago and replies at once. Nothing reaches the servers.
The user types 'cak'. This prefix is rarer and not cached, so the CDN passes the request to the load balancer.
The load balancer picks the shard that owns prefixes starting with a to c, one of several replicas of it.
The shard follows three links in its in-memory trie, c then a then k, and reads the top five already stored at that node. No scanning, no sorting. A blocklist check removes anything not allowed.
The answer travels back through the CDN, which keeps it for a few minutes for the next person typing 'cak'.
The user presses Enter. The search itself runs elsewhere, but the query is written to the search log. This is the only part of the whole flow that touches the data.
Every hour the builder counts the logs, rebuilds the tries, drops blocked queries and writes new snapshots. The shards load them in the background and switch over in one step.
